transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (NexaSearch), Aisha Rahman (Nexa CTO), Connor Briggs (SRE), Samir Dutta (Data Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Customer evaluating pilot to replace in-house vector infra; main goals: stable latency, reduce cost per query, evaluate Redwood Dedicated vs Private for compliance.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jamie, AE at Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya (Nexa): Maya here, head of search.
[00:10] Aisha (Nexa): Aisha, CTO.
[00:12] Connor (Nexa): Connor, SRE.
[00:14] Samir (Nexa): Samir, data eng.
[00:16] Ravi (Redwood SE): Ravi here, SE, I'll take the deep technical bits.
[00:19] Jamie: Great. High level we want to understand your current retrieval + rerank flow, qps, latency targets, and security constraints so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private. Maya, do you want to kick off?
[00:30] Maya: Sure. So we run a hybrid search right now. We do a cheap ANN lookup in our vector DB, then we run a reranker LLM for top 20 results. The issue is throughput, right now our in-house nodes start to choke at about 80 rps for the rerank model and latency jumps. We want a pilot to see if Redwood can get us to 200 rps sustained with p99 under 150ms for the rerank step. Also, regulatory asks mean some corp data cannot leave our VPC.
[00:55] Jamie: Got it. Two numbers to keep in mind: your desired QPS for search, and the p99 for rerank. Can you confirm your typical embedding dimension and model?
[01:05] Maya: We currently use 512-dim embeddings generated with an open encoder. We're also experimenting with a 1K dim model for better recall, but cost is creeping up.
[01:15] Ravi: Quick clarifying — that 150ms p99 is end-to-end or just the LLM rerank?
[01:18] Maya: That's for the rerank call only, so after the ANN shortlist. The ANN step is separately tuned.
[01:22] Ravi: Okay, good. For rerank-only p99 targets, Redwood has a few levers: batching, prefix cache, and quantization-friendly model variants. For 512 dims that's pretty sweet — we can get tight KV cache behavior and lower per-token work.
[01:40] Samir: When you say KV cache, do you mean the model's key/value attention cache or some external cache?
[01:44] Ravi: The KV cache is the internal key/value state we keep across tokens. But also we do prefix caching so if your rerank prompts share long repeated context we cache those embeddings and token outputs. Sometimes fireflies transcription says "kay vee" — um, spelled KV.
[01:58] Connor: On the DB side, we currently run Milvus on k8s. It's sharded per shard. Latency for the ANN search is under 20ms typically. The issue is the LLM stage and network hop between our VPC and the rerank endpoint.
[02:12] Elena: For network hops we have a few patterns: 1) keep vector DB on the customer's side and call Redwood endpoints (you'd use Private/VPC deployment), 2) you push vectors to Redwood-hosted vector overlay and we handle both retrieval and rerank, or 3) hybrid — host vectors in your DB but replicate top-K into Redwood cache for rerank.
[02:35] Maya: We're interested in hybrid because we can't move all vectors off-prem. How does replication work? Is it eventual? Consistency?
[02:42] Ravi: Good question. Typically we do an incremental sync of the top-k index materialized into an LRU cache in Redwood's network edge — it's eventual, configurable TTL. You get near real-time for most use cases. For strict compliance we keep metadata pointers only and call your DB via private networking.
[02:59] Aisha: From a compliance POV, what are the guarantees for audit logs and KMS? We need to show SOC2 controls and that keys are customer-managed.
[03:07] Jamie: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and Dedicated with HSM integrations for enterprise tiers. Audit logs are available — per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdown in the Console. We'll push the SOC2 and architecture doc after the call.
[03:20] Maya: Good. On performance, can you quantify how dimensionality affects throughput? If we move to 1024 dims, what's the cost and latency impact?
[03:28] Ravi: Short answer: dims scale compute and memory — roughly linear-ish for nearest-neighbor compute but the rerank LLM cost doesn't change with embedding dims unless you use embeddings inside the prompt. For ANN lookups, doubling dims can double index size and search cost, which affects end-to-end latency if you host the ANN. If Redwood hosts ANN and rerank, we can optimize kernels, but cost will go up.
[03:55] Samir: Would you recommend lowering dims and increasing recall with better model architecture instead?
[04:00] Elena: Often it's better to pick an embedding model that gives the best ROC@k for a given dim. Sometimes you get more signal from better encoders at 512 dims than naive 1K dims. We can run evaluations during the pilot.
[04:12] Maya: Pilot shape? What do you suggest?
[04:15] Jamie: Here's a pragmatic pilot: 2-week data sync + profiling, run 512-dim baseline on Redwood-hosted rerank endpoints with your Milvus shortlist, measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per query; then a second wave with dedicated reserved nodes and a 1024-dim test. If compliance requires, swap out to a Private VPC run for the rerank endpoints only.
[04:40] Connor: How are fallbacks handled? If Dedicated capacity gets saturated, will we see dropped requests?
[04:44] Ravi: We have smart routing and automatic fallback policies. For Dedicated you can configure burst capacity and a fallback to compatible hosted variants. We also do circuit breakers to avoid full outages — typically responses degrade to lower-fidelity model before failing.
[04:58] Maya: What's the expected cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for our anticipated 200rps?
[05:03] Jamie: We'll share the exact numbers, but qualitatively Dedicated tends to lower unit cost at sustained throughput because reserved capacity amortizes GPU cost. Hosted is better for spikes and faster onboarding. We'll attach a sample math sheet in the follow-up.
[05:18] Samir: A technical question: for rerank we send top-20 with full context in prompt. That means token lengths can be quite variable. How does Redwood handle long prompts? Any prompt truncation or streaming?
[05:30] Ravi: We support streaming and structured output. For long prompts we rely on kernel optimizations and KV cache to reduce repeated compute. Also, you can do chunked rerank or pairwise rerank to reduce tokens per call. We'll model that in the perf estimate.
[05:45] Aisha: For private deployments, what does the control plane look like? Is there telemetry back to Redwood?
[05:50] Jamie: In Private mode the control plane can be customer-controlled; telemetry can be sent to your observability endpoint or retained within the VPC. Audit logs still exist and we can offer an offline export for compliance reviews.
[06:03] Maya: Any hard limits on batch size for continuous batching in the runtime? We saw some doc blips about 256 token batches causing memory spikes.
[06:12] Ravi: There are practical limits based on GPU memory and sequence length. We tune bin-packing and batching windows by workload. If your rerank calls are short (few tokens) we can micro-batch aggressively. We'll need sample distributions to tune correctly.
[06:28] Connor: Network latency between our Milvus cluster in GCP and Redwood's hosted endpoints — is there a recommended topology?
[06:34] Elena: Best is to colocate in same region and use VPC peering or HPC interconnect where possible. For sensitive networks you can put Redwood within your VPC via private deployment. For hybrid we often recommend an edge cache to avoid cross-network round trips for the rerank stage.
[06:52] Samir: How do you handle vector format mismatches? We currently use float32 raw vectors; some vendors recommend uint8 quantization.
[06:59] Ravi: Redwood ingestion accepts common serializations; we also support on-the-fly PQ or 8-bit quantization for storage optimization. But quantization changes similarity quality, so we recommend running recall-resilience evals. We'll provide tooling for quantization-aware evals.
[07:12] Maya: Any built-in rerank metrics? We want to monitor A/B lifts and regression.
[07:17] Jamie: Console includes eval decks and you can wire in your own A/B logic. We have quality-monitoring tied to prompt sets so you get regression alerts if recall drops.
[07:28] Aisha: Does Redwood support SAML SSO for team access and RBAC? We need audit-friendly admin controls.
[07:33] Jamie: Yes, SAML/SSO, SCIM, fine-grained RBAC, and per-route policies are standard on enterprise plans.
[07:41] Connor: Ok, let's talk pilot data volume — we have about 20M vectors, but only 2M are "active" for the search space. How would you approach indexing?
[07:51] Ravi: Typically we suggest sharding by namespace of actives, and using a TTL/compact policy for cold vectors. For the pilot we can ingest only the 2M actives and do a background sync for the rest if needed. That keeps cost and memory bounded.
[08:08] Samir: Are replicas supported for high availability in Dedicated? We need HA for production.
[08:12] Elena: Yes, Dedicated supports multi-AZ replicas, and Private deployments can be configured for HA with your infra team.
[08:19] Maya: Question on data residency — can we pin storage to specific regions for GDPR?
[08:23] Jamie: Yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted defaults to region nearest to customer but you can choose region restriction on enterprise plans.
[08:32] Maya: For the pilot, what telemetry will you need from us?
[08:36] Ravi: A sample of queries (100k-200k) with token length distribution, current index size and dimension, and QPS timelines (peak and sustained) plus sample latency traces. That will let us produce an accurate perf estimate.
[08:50] Maya: We can do that. We'll anonymize data where needed.
[08:53] Jamie: Great. Any blockers on the compliance side?
[08:55] Aisha: We need customer-managed KMS or HSM, SOC2 docs, and a network diagram for the Private option. Also need to know if logs contain PII — we need controls to redact or keep logs in-customer.
[09:07] Elena: We can redact logs and support customer-controlled retention. For KMS we support customer-managed keys in Private and on some enterprise Dedicated tiers. We'll attach the SOC2 + security appendix.
[09:18] Samir: One more — latency modelling. Can you give a back-of-envelope for rerank-only at 200rps with 512 dims?
[09:24] Ravi: Back-of-envelope: with optimized kernels and micro-batching we can aim for p50 ~30-40ms, p95 ~80-120ms, p99 ~120-180ms depending on token lengths and burstiness. That's for hosted with caching. Dedicated tuned with reserved GPUs will tighten that and lower cost per q. We'll produce a modeled table.
[09:45] Connor: Good. Anything about data residency for replicas?
[09:48] Jamie: We'll include region replication options in the write-up.
[09:52] Maya: Okay let's get next steps and owners.
[09:55] Jamie: Recap: Jamie will send pricing + pilot SOW; Ravi will run perf estimate; Maya & Samir to send sample payloads; Connor to share network diagrams and KMS constraints; then we set up a deep-dive demo targeted for week of July 20th.
[10:12] Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks.
[10:14] Jamie: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck and docs.
